summary: Vitals Check is a web app that helps astronauts assess their own health on long missions, when help from the ground can be slow. Crew log eight readings (heart rate, blood pressure, blood sugar, temperature, sleep, mood, exercise, and nutrition), or estimate their pulse with a device camera. A clickable body map and colour-coded status show what is in range. Trend Watch warns when a reading is drifting towards a limit. Each reading comes with plain guidance on why it matters in space, how to measure it and what to do. A daily routine with reminders keeps checks regular. A one-tap report summarises status for the flight surgeon, adjusted for station, Moon or Mars communication delays. It is built around NASA’s five hazards of human spaceflight.
details:
Vitals Check is a self-assessment tool for astronauts on long-duration missions. Crew logs eight indicators: heart rate, blood pressure, blood sugar, temperature, sleep, mood, exercise, and nutrition. They can also estimate pulse from a fingertip over the device camera. Each reading is colour-coded green, amber or red, and one banner shows the worst status. A clickable body map groups readings by region. Each reading includes why it matters in space, how to measure it, what to do, and the basis for its range. Trend Watch projects recent changes forward and warns before a reading reaches a limit. A daily routine with reminders keeps checks regular. A one-tap report summarises status for the flight surgeon and states the ground reply delay for a space station, lunar base or Mars mission.

We organised the readings around NASA’s five hazards of human spaceflight, so each hazard maps to the indicators that reveal its effects. We considered limited crew time, delayed communication, and astronauts who are not medical experts, so every screen leads with the action to take.

The benefit is earlier detection and clearer self-care when ground support is delayed. We expect it to help crews notice drift in sleep, exercise, or nutrition before it becomes a health problem.

It is a static web app in HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. It has no server; readings stay on the device, and it is hosted on Netlify. The camera pulse uses the browser camera API. The slide deck was made with PptxGenJS.

Limits: the ranges are simplified and are not medical guidance. Sleep and exercise targets draw on published research, and the remaining ranges are standard adult clinical references. The camera pulse is a rough estimate. Real use would need flight-surgeon-approved limits.
